title: Write in terms of $$y=2^x$$
text:
First express each term in terms of $$2^x$$ using laws of exponents: $$a**{bc}=(a**b)**c$$ and $$a**{b+c}=a**b a**c.$$ 

$$2**{3x}-2**{x+2}=(2**x)**3-(2**x)(2**2)=48$$ 
 Next substitute $$y$$ in for $$2^x$$ everywhere: 

$$\left(2^xight)^3-2^x 2^2=y^3-4y=48$$

title: Find a clever solution
text: Solving cubics by hand is tricky! In this case, the algebra is telling us we can factor $$48$$ into a product of $$3$$ numbers that differ by $$2$$. That factorization is $$(2)(4)(6)=48$$. $$So$$ $$\left(y-2\right) y\left(y+2\right)=(2)(4)(6), $$ or $$y=4$$.
